newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Shell Australia says shutdown depletes stocks.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Shell Australia says shutdown depletes stocks.

text.p: The Shell Co of Australia Ltd said petrol stocks have been depleted following a longer than expected maintenance shutdown of the catalytic cracker at its Clyde refinery in Sydney.
A Shell spokesman said the 5,500 tonnes-per-day (50,000 barrels-per-day) cracker was restarted eight days ago, but had been down for about 11 weeks, two weeks longer than planned.
"The result of that was that we have had stock shortages," he said. "We haven't been able to supply our own network and our customers in other companies."
The shortages had affected petrol prices in Sydney which had risen during the Christmas period, with some stations running out of petrol, he said.
Shell supplies about 40 percent of the New South Wales petrol market.
The spokesman said the 80,000 bpd refinery was now able to begin distribution, and stocks were expected to return to normal levels throughout the system towards the end of January.
"The worst of the problem is over and things are likely to improve from now on," he said.
A catalytic refiner is a secondary refining unit which breaks down heavy residual fuels into lighter distillates such as gasoline, jet fuel and diesel.
